name: LEEP's Malawi lead paint programme (LEEP's own CEA, January 2022)
beneficiaries_note: The model's name: LEEP's Malawi lead paint programme (LEEP's own CEA, January 2022).

missing_data.note: Thin: LEEP's projection of a regulation it had just helped start: the homes left unpainted with lead paint, the children spared and their health and earnings are modelled, not measured.

summary: The Lead Exposure Elimination Project tested paint on sale in Malawi, found high lead levels and brought the results to the Malawi Bureau of Standards, which began enforcing its existing lead paint standard; LEEP then helped the four local manufacturers switch. LEEP's own analysis credits it with bringing enforcement forward by eight years and counts the children spared paint lead over the next 20 years: their health (from the Global Burden of Disease) and their later earnings. Our view keeps LEEP's costs, children and health years and values the earnings with the site's shared figures for blood lead, IQ points per µg/dL and earnings per IQ point.

resources.note: The figures this model reproduces. LEEP's model itself was built in Causal (a modelling tool), which no longer shows it without signing in, and the January 2022 documentation needs a Google sign-in, so the model is built from the totals stated on this page, each quoted on its row.

resources.title: LEEP, LEEP cost-effectiveness analysis - Malawi (2021 documentation)
resources.note: The first version's documentation (April 2021, $12 per DALY-equivalent): how the model counts children newly exposed to lead paint, the 20% paint share, Attina and Trasande's earnings losses halved to 1% per IQ point, 2.8 years of income per DALY, the 4% discount rate and the 20-year wait until benefits are felt.

sections.title: LEEP's estimate (January 2022)
sections.explainer: LEEP compares two futures for Malawi: lead paint regulation enforced after one year (with LEEP) or after nine (without), so LEEP brings it forward by eight years. In each, children are newly exposed to lead paint every year in proportion to the homes painted with unregulated paint; the difference over 20 years is LEEP's impact. Health comes from the Global Burden of Disease's DALYs for lead, earnings from Attina and Trasande's estimate of lost income in low- and middle-income countries, both cut to the 20% of children's lead LEEP puts down to paint. Costs and benefits are discounted at 4% a year.

sections.title: Health: deaths valued by age
sections.explainer: charityevals' step. LEEP's health years are the Global Burden of Disease's DALYs for lead: mostly years of life lost to heart disease and kidney disease in adults, at GBD's life expectancy, untouched by the value-of-life slider. Our view splits each into the illness part and the deaths behind the rest, valued by age like every death on the site.

sections.title: Earnings, valued the site's way
sections.explainer: charityevals' step. LEEP values the earnings with its own conversions: Attina and Trasande's lost income per child, halved to 1% per IQ point, and 2.8 years of income per DALY. The site answers each of these questions once for every model: the blood lead of a typical child in these countries and the IQ points lost per µg/dL (facts: lead), the earnings gain per IQ point, the years it lasts and the household sharing (facts: givewell_shared), and the value of a gain in income (Your values). Our view applies them to LEEP's own count of children spared.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not LEEP's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost.

sections.title: Bottom line
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not LEEP's: LEEP's cost per DALY-equivalent, with the health and earnings parts valued the site's way.

source.quote: Our calculations show that, over the first 20 years, we can expect to avert ~43,000 DALY-equivalents in Malawi.

rows.explainer: LEEP counts the lead exposure averted over 20 years from when regulation is implemented, which its 2021 documentation calls a subjective choice, short for paint that lasts decades in homes.

source.title: LEEP, How Cost-Effective Is LEEP's Malawi Program?
source.page: How cost-effective is LEEP's Malawi program?

rows.explainer: LEEP's assumption: the standard enforced after one year with LEEP, after nine without.

rows.label: Years enforcement is brought forward
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. LEEP credits itself with eight years of earlier enforcement. Every model that credits a won reform reads one figure for how long the win counts before it would have come anyway: Years a won reform counts, under Your values (5 by default, 1–20). The evaluator view keeps LEEP's eight.

rows.label: Years brought forward, as a share of LEEP's eight
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. LEEP publishes totals, not its yearly rows, so our view scales the children spared, the health years and the government's enforcement spending in proportion to the years brought forward. An approximation: the first years brought forward are discounted least and the paint stays on walls for a fixed time, so the true figure doesn't move exactly in proportion. LEEP's own spending and its 20 years of averted exposure stay as they are. 100% in the evaluator view.

rows.label: Average wait from exposure averted to benefits felt

source.quote: We estimate that on average benefits to health and income will be felt 20 years in the future from the time childhood lead exposure is averted

rows.explainer: Some benefits come sooner (intellectual disability), the earnings later, once the children reach working age.

rows.label: Health years gained per year of averted exposure, before discounting

source.title: LEEP, How Cost-Effective Is LEEP's Malawi Program?
source.page: How cost-effective is LEEP's Malawi program?
source.quote: Of these, improved health outcomes account for about 20% (~8,000 DALYs averted)

rows.explainer: Derived from LEEP's stated total, so the discounting can follow the shared rate: LEEP's 8,000 discounted DALYs spread evenly over its 20 years of averted exposure, each felt 20 years later, at LEEP's 4% (8,000 ÷ 6.4505). LEEP's yearly profile rises to a peak and then tapers as regulation would have come anyway; it isn't published, so an even spread stands in for it.

rows.label: Health years gained (DALYs averted), discounted
rows.explainer: The Global Burden of Disease 2019's DALYs for lead exposure (intellectual disability, heart disease, kidney disease), for the children spared paint lead, discounted at the shared rate (LEEP's 4% in the evaluator view). LEEP's figure: about 8,000, which it likens to lead poisoning averted in about 215,000 children.

rows.label: Earnings gained, in LEEP's DALY-equivalents, discounted

source.title: LEEP, How Cost-Effective Is LEEP's Malawi Program?
source.page: How cost-effective is LEEP's Malawi program?
source.quote: while increased income accounts for the other 80% (~35,000 DALY-equivalents averted)

rows.explainer: About $180 million of lifetime earnings the children keep, from Attina and Trasande (2013), halved because LEEP assumes 1% more earnings per IQ point rather than the study's 2%, and converted at 2.8 years of income per DALY (from GiveWell's 2019 moral weights). Our view values the earnings itself (section below).

rows.label: DALY-equivalents averted over 20 years, discounted
Cost per DALY-equivalent averted
rows.explainer: LEEP's bottom line: "$14 per DALY-equivalent averted", the median of its Monte Carlo simulations. The totals it states give $13.7, which rounds to the same figure.

rows.label: Value of a heart-disease death averted, at the world's ages, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The ages of the world's cardiovascular deaths (facts: death_ages) valued by GiveWell's weights by age, the 70-and-over band split by the share at 80 or older, times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years at Your values' exchange rate. Lead's deaths are mostly heart disease in older adults.

rows.label: Our value of one of LEEP's GBD DALYs (deaths valued by age), per DALY
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** LEEP counts the Global Burden of Disease's DALYs for lead. Our view splits each DALY into the illness part (kept as DALYs) and the deaths behind the rest, at heart disease's ratio (GBD 2023, world), and values those deaths by age like every death on the site (row above). Heart disease stands in for all of lead's burden; the small intellectual-disability part is treated the same way. The evaluator view keeps LEEP's DALYs (1).

rows.label: Health years gained, deaths valued by age
rows.explainer: Scaled to the years enforcement is brought forward in our view (brought_forward_scale).

rows.label: Children spared lead poisoning from paint over the 20 years

source.title: LEEP, How Cost-Effective Is LEEP's Malawi Program?
source.page: How cost-effective is LEEP's Malawi program?
source.quote: ~8,000 DALYs roughly represents lead poisoning being averted in ~215,000 fewer children in Malawi over the course of the next 20 years

rows.explainer: LEEP's count, the reach its health and earnings figures rest on: children newly exposed each year (IHME's 3.4 million Malawian children above 5 µg/dL, one year's cohort of them), times the 20% of children's lead LEEP puts down to paint, times the growth in homes painted with unregulated paint, compared between enforcement after one year and after nine. Each counted child stands for a whole childhood of lead poisoning from paint.

rows.label: Children spared, discounted to today
rows.explainer: LEEP's children spread evenly over its 20 years, each year's discounted at the shared rate, scaled to the years enforcement is brought forward in our view (brought_forward_scale).

rows.label: Blood lead of a typical child in low- and middle-income countries
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: lead), 5 µg/dL. LEEP's children are those above IHME's 5 µg/dL threshold, so their own average is likely higher; the shared figure keeps the step the same as in our other lead models.

rows.label: IQ points lost per µg/dL of children's blood lead
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: lead): 0.5 a µg/dL from the seven-cohort pooled analysis between 2.4 and 10 µg/dL (Lanphear et al. 2005), the analysis Attina and Trasande's lost-income figures also build on.

rows.label: IQ points a child keeps when spared
Increase in earnings per IQ point
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** LEEP assumes 1% more earnings per IQ point (halving Attina and Trasande's 2%, "consistent with GiveWell"); the site uses GiveWell's current figure for every model, 0.67% (facts: givewell_shared).

rows.label: Household sharing multiplier on an earnings gain
rows.explainer: The shared multiplier for later-life income gains shared within the household (facts: givewell_shared). LEEP counts the earner's income only.

rows.label: Years an IQ gain raises earnings, discounted
rows.explainer: The shared working life of 40 years (facts: givewell_shared.long_term_benefit_years), discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Years from a child's exposure to working age
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: lead): lead harms the brain most before about age six (exposure centred near age three), and earnings start at about 20. LEEP puts the average wait for all benefits at 20 years.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the earnings gain begins
Earnings kept by the children spared, in units of value
rows.formula: children_spared_pv * iq_points_per_child * iq_wage_gain * resource_sharing * iq_years * income_wait_discount * $uov_per_ln_consumption
rows.explainer: The IQ points kept, as a gain in ln(consumption) over the working life, shared in the household, after the wait, valued at Your values' value of a gain in income.

rows.label: Earnings kept, in healthy years
rows.explainer: At Your values' exchange rate between income and health (LEEP's 2.8 years of income per DALY in the evaluator view).

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; LEEP's 2022 cost split isn't in the analysis.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same work, as a share of LEEP's DALY-equivalents
rows.explainer: The health years with deaths valued by age plus the earnings valued the site's way, over LEEP's 43,000. The evaluator view keeps LEEP's (1).

rows.label: Share of LEEP's cost figure that is the government's enforcement spending (counted at half)
rows.explainer: Computed from the flows LEEP states: its own $80,000 a year for five years and the Malawi Bureau of Standards' $75,000 a year for eight, discounted at 4% a year, the government's counted at half: about $250,000 of about $610,000, 41.5% whether the years are discounted from their start or their end. The stated flows add to $609,000 to $633,000 against LEEP's published $590,000, so the split is an estimate; the range covers that gap.

rows.label: Cost LEEP counts per dollar of its own (the government's spending leaves the cost)
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Malawi Bureau of Standards, which enforces the standard, carries out the work only because of the charity, so they are credited through the share below (mobiliser_share), not by counting their money in the cost (docs/normalization.md 2.24): counted in both, they would be cut twice. The evaluator view keeps LEEP's cost (1).

rows.label: Share of the government's enforcement spending that LEEP counts as a cost
rows.explainer: LEEP's own rule: it counts government money at half, as that money would otherwise be spent less well (its 2021 documentation). Used here only to get back to the spending in full.

rows.label: Government's enforcement spending, at what the money would otherwise have done, as a share of the good done
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The government's enforcement spending in full, for the years enforcement is brought forward (LEEP's eight years of spending times brought_forward_scale), valued at GiveWell's figure for what a dollar a government in its programme countries spends would otherwise have done (@givewell_shared.cf_value_government, about 1.5 times cash), the site's one figure for redirected government money (docs/normalization.md 2.20), over our healthy years gained. A cost of the resources LEEP mobilises: netted from the good before the mobiliser's share. The evaluator view counts half the spending in the cost instead (0 here).

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar
rows.formula: ((1 / cost_per_daly_equivalent) * ours_vs_leep * donor_cost_share) * adopter_cost_out * (1 - gov_cost_share_of_good) * mobiliser_share
rows.explainer:
LEEP's DALY-equivalents per dollar of the cost it counts, valued the site's way, per dollar of LEEP's own spending (adopter_cost_out), net of what the government's enforcement money would otherwise have done, times the charity's share of the good that others carry out (mobiliser_share).

With credit by share of resources on, times the share of LEEP's full cost paid in cash.
